blurb: `consumes payment` brings every type that `payment` exports into scope under its own name, because the services' signatures use them. If this context already has something of that name, a type declared here or reached through `uses`, or a function, asset, service, agent or provider, a mention would mean two things, so the compiler refuses the clause. Rename the imported type with `as`: it is then in scope only under the alias, and is still the same type. `bynk.consumes.type_alias_conflict` is the same clash with an alias.
summary: A `consumes` name collides with another name in scope.
